DOCUMENT AI · OFFICIAL-SOURCE REVIEW

MarkItDown

Microsoft 的 Python 工具，把多种文件和 Office 文档转换为更适合 LLM 消费的 Markdown。

Microsoft's Python utility for converting files and Office documents into LLM-friendly Markdown.

结论：这是六项中用途最窄、也最容易验证价值的工具。适合 RAG 入库、搜索索引和文档批处理，但“能转”不等于“信息无损”，表格、扫描件、复杂版式与恶意文件必须单独测试。
Verdict: This is the narrowest—and easiest to evaluate—tool in the watchlist. It fits RAG ingestion, search indexing and document batches, but successful conversion does not guarantee fidelity across tables, scans, complex layouts or hostile files.

为什么会成为 AI 基础工具？

LLM 和检索系统更容易消费结构清晰的文本。MarkItDown 把 PDF、Word、PowerPoint、Excel、HTML 等输入统一成 Markdown，减少每种格式单独接入的工作。官方包要求 Python 3.10 及以上，并以可选依赖支持不同文件类型。

它的价值来自“足够好的标准化”，而不是像素级复刻原文。若任务依赖表格单元格、脚注、阅读顺序或精确布局，仍需保留原文件并建立对照测试。

为什么是 76 分？

Why is it useful AI infrastructure?

LLMs and retrieval systems consume structured text more easily. MarkItDown converts PDFs, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML and other inputs into Markdown, reducing one-off integration work. Its official package requires Python 3.10+ and uses optional dependencies for formats.

The value is useful normalization, not pixel-perfect reproduction. Workflows that depend on cell structure, footnotes, reading order or layout still need source retention and comparison tests.

真正应该怎么测？

  • 建立包含正文、表格、图片、扫描页、脚注和异常编码的固定样本集。
  • 同时检查文本召回率、阅读顺序、表格结构和转换耗时，而不是只看文件是否生成。
  • 在隔离环境解析未知来源文件，并限制文件大小、页数、超时和内存。
  • 区分纯本地转换、OCR 插件和调用视觉模型的路径及其数据流向。

来源与边界

格式、运行条件和插件信息来自 Microsoft 官方仓库；指标来自 GitHub REST API。尚未使用统一文档集做质量基准，初评置信度 70%。

How should it be tested?

  • Build a stable corpus with prose, tables, images, scans, footnotes and broken encodings.
  • Measure text recall, reading order, table structure and time—not merely file creation.
  • Parse untrusted files in isolation with size, page, timeout and memory limits.
  • Separate local conversion, OCR plugins and vision-model paths and their data flows.

Sources and limits

Formats, runtime requirements and plugins come from the official repository. Metrics come from the GitHub REST API. No standardized document-quality benchmark yet; confidence is 70%.
